reason: Quote under the release question states a released BYOIP Elastic IP goes back to the BYOIP IP pool it was allocated from.
Quote states the BYOIP prefix can be used with any number of VPCs in the same account.
Quote states a maximum of five IP ranges can be brought to the account.
Quote gives /24 for IPv4 and /56 for IPv6 as most specific, with /48 for internet-advertised IPv6 carried in the condition qualifier.
Quote says a prefix is moved by de-provisioning it from the current Region and provisioning it in the new one.
Quote lists customer whitelisting as a reason: moving allow-listed workloads without re-establishing the lists.
Quote states BYOIP moves all or part of publicly routable IPv4 or IPv6 space to AWS and customers keep owning the range.
Bullet under connectivity options lists other AWS services via internet gateway, NAT, virtual private gateway or VPC endpoints.
Quote states instances in subnets in different Availability Zones are charged $0.01 per GB for data transfer; the claim adds nothing beyond it.
Quote lists inter-Region peering, public IPs, NAT gateway, NAT instances, VPN and Direct Connect for cross-Region instance communication.
Component list defines the egress-only internet gateway as a stateful gateway for egress-only IPv6 access to the internet.
Component list defines the internet gateway as the VPC side of a connection to the public internet.
Component list defines the NAT gateway as a highly available managed NAT service for private-subnet resources to reach the internet.
Component list defines a subnet as a segment of the VPC IP range for groups of isolated resources.
Component list defines the virtual private gateway as the VPC side of a VPN connection.
Component list defines a VPC as a logically isolated virtual network whose address space you define from ranges you select.
Component list defines VPC endpoints as private connectivity to AWS-hosted services without IGW, VPN, NAT or firewall proxies.
Quote says a default route can be created for each subnet, directing egress via the internet gateway, virtual private gateway or NAT gateway.
Heading asks about adding subnets such as private subnets to the default VPC; the answer is yes and names the console or --subnet option.
Quote states the default VPC is created automatically the first time EC2 resources are provisioned and launches without a subnet ID go there.
Heading asks whether EIPs can be assigned to VPC instances; answer yes, but reachable only from the internet, not over VPN.
Quote states EIPs should be used only in subnets routing directly to the IGW and cannot be used behind NAT gateway or NAT instance; context limits to IPv4.
Quote states Enforce mode prevents creating or attaching resources allowing unencrypted traffic and blocks instances without native Nitro encryption.
Two quotes give the definition (centralized monitor and enforce of encryption within and across VPCs in a Region) and the Monitor and Enforce modes.
Quotes name gateway and interface endpoint types and say gateway endpoints are only for AWS services including S3 and DynamoDB, adding a route table entry; claim is scoped to the FAQ.
Quote states endpoints connect privately without IGW, NAT, VPN or proxies and are horizontally scalable, highly available virtual devices.
Quote says this is not the use case best suited for multiple interfaces and recommends extra private IPs with EIPs.
Quote states network interfaces can only be attached to instances in VPCs in the same account.
Quote states network interfaces can only be attached to instances in the same Availability Zone.
Quote names CloudWatch Log Insights or Contributor Insights and Athena or AWS QuickSight; the claim's 'Amazon Quick (formerly QuickSight)' renaming is not in the quote.
Quote states charges from publishing flow logs can be tracked using cost allocation tags.
Quote states flow logs can be created or deleted without any risk of impact to network performance.
Quote states enriched metadata shows who initiated TCP connections and the packet-level source and destination through layers such as the NAT gateway.
Quote states a flow log subscription chooses metadata fields, maximum aggregation interval and log destination.
Quote states a flow log can be created for a Transit Gateway or an individual Transit Gateway attachment.
In context 'this feature' is flow logs; quote says it troubleshoots connectivity and security issues and checks access rules work.
Two quotes list visibility into dependencies and patterns, anomaly detection, data-leak prevention, troubleshooting, and archiving for compliance.
Quotes list the flow-log metadata fields and say traffic mirroring lets you analyze actual traffic content including payload.
Quote states the internet gateway lets EC2 instances directly access the internet and the egress-only IGW is stateful, egress-only for IPv6.
Quote states you must specify the subnet at launch and the instance is launched in that subnet's Availability Zone.
